correctness.rationale: For every prefix of length k the residual is either constant (if b^k does not divide c+1+u) or V_{s,k mod m} (if divisible). Exactly one u per depth satisfies divisibility, with s=ceil((c+1)/b^k). These s decrease strictly until 1 at L_b(c), thereafter providing precisely m phase states; all m constants are reached by digit 0 from V_{1,p}. The explicit transition recursion constructs a total DFAO. Distinguish different shifts s,t via continuations b^r-s at r and r+1; valuation of b^r+t-s stays fixed for r>nu_b(|t-s|) while valuation of b^r changes by one modulo m. This handles composite bases and proves genuine minimality, not just a finite test. The extracted standard-library checker independently minimized 3200 reachable DFAs and checked 204800 direct outputs.

None of the material inspected identifies the modular valuation-residue residual graph or the exact base-b/minimum modulus-m shifted-state law. Targeted mathematical web searches and multiple research-record comparisons found no stronger or equivalent valuation-residue shift theorem. The nearest same-period-doubling research records address attractors or dynamical components, not automaton state count. Search absence alone is not treated as proof of global novelty; unindexed historical equivalence remains a risk.

value.rationale: Determines the exact minimal-state complexity and complete residual graph for an infinite three-parameter family of automatic valuation words, including every translate of the classical period-doubling word. It sharpens the current general state-complexity question for shifts from a bound to an exact formula, shows the exact logarithmic coefficient one and additive residue penalty two m, and identifies every power-of-base transition. This is a natural automata-theoretic invariant motivated by the recent shift-state literature, not an arbitrary finite census; the all-moduli proof and minimality graph are substantive. No claim of improving worst-case complexity for unrelated automatic words is made.
